_comment: The Helm chart delivery option every new version of the AWS Marketplace container product gets (Catalog API, AddDeliveryOptions; automation/aws_catalog.py). AWS fills ${AWSMP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT} with the service account its launch page has the buyer create with an IAM role: the chart runs OneUptime as it (serviceAccount.name), and reports usage with that role. Usage instructions: at most 4,000 characters.
title: Helm chart for Amazon EKS
description: OneUptime Enterprise on Amazon EKS, installed with Helm: uptime monitoring, status pages, on-call, incidents, logs, traces and metrics in one platform, with its own PostgreSQL, ClickHouse and Valkey in the cluster. Guide: https://oneuptime.com/docs/installation/cloud-marketplaces
usageInstructions:
Before you install:
1. An Amazon EKS cluster with at least 3 nodes of 4 vCPUs and 16 GiB of memory, the Amazon EBS CSI driver with a default StorageClass, and an IAM OIDC provider:
   eksctl utils associate-iam-oidc-provider --cluster <cluster> --approve
2. Create the IAM role and the Kubernetes service account with the eksctl command on this page. OneUptime reports its users to AWS Marketplace every hour with it; without it, the Enterprise features stay off.

Install with the helm command on this page. In it, set host to your domain name (for example oneuptime.example.com), and httpProtocol to https if a certificate is in front of OneUptime.

Then point the domain name at the load balancer (the EXTERNAL-IP of the service ending in -nginx: kubectl get service --namespace oneuptime) and open it to create the first account. The first start migrates the database and takes a few minutes. Within the hour, the dashboard's edition label shows the Enterprise Edition, licensed through AWS Marketplace.

To upgrade, run helm upgrade with a newer version of this chart and the same values.

Guide: https://oneuptime.com/docs/installation/cloud-marketplaces
Support: https://oneuptime.com/support
